This plan improves the supplied parent construction by attacking the overlap problem through a mathematically safe convex majorant, while using exact evaluator scoring for every accepted candidate. The central idea is not to minimize the nonconvex evaluator objective directly, nor to rely on a single black-box nonlinear solver. The plan has two principal, cooperating layers:

- First, minimize a convex quadratic majorant of the evaluator objective, without claiming that it gives a lower bound for the true optimum. Regardless, any feasible vector whose majorant is small is a certified feasible upper bound for the true objective because of the pointwise Young inequality:
  \[
  h_i(1-h_j) \le \frac{h_i^2+(1-h_j)^2}{2}.

Floating arithmetic may need exact repair, but this is much stronger than the standard constant-plus-project projection.
